newsitem.title: USA: Former US soldier indicted on spying charges.
newsitem.headline: Former US soldier indicted on spying charges.

text.p: U.S. agents arrested a former U.S. Army clerk on Tuesday on charges that she spied for communist countries while based in Germany during the Cold War years, justice officials said.

Among documents Kelly Therese Warren, 31, allegedly gave to a U.S. Army sergeant to pass to Hungarian and Czech agents were secret U.S. and NATO plans for the defence of Western Europe in case of a Soviet bloc attack, the indictment said.

Warren, of Warner-Robbins, Georgia, was the fifth person to be charged in connection with the spy ring as result of a 10-year probe by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Army intelligence. Four others, including the sergeant and ringleader, Clyde Lee Conrad, are serving long jail terms.

Warren served in the 8th Infantry Division headquarters at Bad Kreuznach, in what was then West Germany, from 1986 to 1988. She worked in the administration of the G-3 Section, where her duties included preparing classified documents for publication and distribution, the indictment said.
G-3 was responsible for planning and training the 8th Infantry for the defence of Western Europe in the event of attack from Warsaw Pact countries.
A spokesman for the U.S. attorney's office in Tampa, David Rhodes, said Warren allegedly passed documents on to Conrad who gave them to the communist agents.
"We are alleging she got paid for it. How much and if there were other motives I can't say," he said.
The conspiracy took place in the summer of 1987 to the spring of 1988, Rhodes added.
Warren, who was arrested in her hometown, was charged with one count of conspiracy to gather and deliver defence. information to a foreign government and two counts of delivering the information.
The two secret documents concerned a counter-attack contingency plan called "Lionheart" and a training exercise relating to the defence of Europe.

"Specifically, indictment alleges that Warren knowingly and wilfully communicated, transmitted and delivered documents and information to representatives and agents of the Peoples Republic of Hungary and the Czechoslovak Socialist Republic which related to the national defence of the United States," the indictment said.

"The indictment further alleges that 8th Infantry Division maintained classified U.S. Army, U.S. Air Forces, and NATO military documents including general defence plans for the use of tactical nuclear weapons by the United States and NATO and chemical warfare documents."
Rhodes was unable to confirm if the documents Warren handed over contained information on nuclear weapons. If found guilty she faces a maximum sentence on life imprisonment.

Conrad was convicted in Germany of spying for Hungary and Czechoslovakia in 1990, two years after he retired. He is now serving life in jail, the toughest sentence handed down by a German court for spying since the end of the Second World War.
Florida judges sentenced Roderick James Ramsay to 36 years imprisonment in 1992 and Jeffrey Rondeau and Jeffrey Gregory to 18 years each in 1994 in connection with the case.
